## Prefer-A draft
conflict_group: path-b-scope-only-activation-verify-ac-before-merge-base-authority
Target-digest: sha256:81b3fc88a87ab4ca8acbc60143da06873883bf87b2cec56b748488f87271c16e
Spec-path: packages/core/src/check + packages/core/src/verify-ac + packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords + write-fence continuity
arc-mode: no-ingest

## In plain English
A consumer can prepare a reviewed scope-only activation brief, but cannot land it: deft check runs the future product acceptance commands and artifact clauses before any product files exist, while the write fence correctly refuses those product writes until the brief is on the merge base. Prefer-A should let a true brief-land-shaped Path B activation clear check without pretending the future product already passes tests, and keep mixed/product diffs on the hard acceptance path.

## Approaches

### Approach A (Prefer-A lean)
Reuse the existing brief-land shape (#5387 isBriefLandShapedDiff: nonterminal xbrief|vbrief under proposed|pending|active plus optional root CHANGELOG.md only). When the selected scope is Path B activation-shaped (productPullRequest unset; working tree / PR diff brief-land only), deft check must not hard-fail verify:ac on missing future product artifacts or on acceptance commands that target those not-yet-landed paths. Record an honest scope-only / activation AC disposition (named skip or deferred-until-product), keep hygiene + scope-provenance membership hard, and require full verify:ac once any product path appears or productPullRequest is set. Share the shape helper rather than inventing a second dialect. Preserve immutable merge-base write-fence authority (no head-brief widen).

### Approach B
Force Path B activation briefs to stamp empty acceptance / none_stated:true and ban derived product commands until a later product restamp. Operators must remember a second acceptance mint after product appears.

### Approach C
Allow first product writes from a pending or head-brief fence so tests can be authored before activation land. Weakens #4956 merge-base immutability.

## Prefer-A
Bind Approach A.

## Reject
Softening verify:ac for mixed scope+product diffs; trusting agent-widened working-tree briefs as write authority; blanket test exemption unrelated to brief-land shape; disabling hooks; inventing a second brief-land path vocabulary beside isBriefLandShapedDiff; Approach C head-brief write authority.

## Draft file_scope (lean)
- packages/core/src/check/cached-orchestrator.ts (and gate admission helpers as needed)
- packages/core/src/verify-ac/** (clause/command gate for activation-shaped selection)
- packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/main.ts (reuse isBriefLandShapedDiff; no second dialect)
- packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts (continuity proof / keep-out of head widen — cite only)
- content/docs/scope-provenance.md (Path B activation AC pointer)
- CHANGELOG.md
- matching unit tests under packages/core/src/check and packages/core/src/verify-ac

## Keep-outs
- #5387 productPullRequest closing-keywords carve (already shipped)
- #5791 framework-only coverageMode (adjacent consumer unblock, different gate)
- #5736 activation/widen PR merge latency
- #4768 acceptance-activate clause derivation refuse
- Weakening product PR verify:ac after product paths exist

## Parent note

## Pain
- P1: Scope-only Path B activation (brief +/- CHANGELOG, productPullRequest unset) fails deft check / verify:ac on missing future product artifacts and acceptance commands before the brief can land.
- P2: Write fence correctly loads file_scope only from merge-base brief bytes, so product source/test writes stay denied until that brief lands — closing the cycle with P1.
- P3: Documented Path B / #5387 brief-land carve does not define an activation-time verify:ac disposition, so operators are pushed toward weakening acceptance, hook bypass, or head-brief write theater.
- P4: Mixed scope+product diffs and same-PR file_scope widening must keep hard verify:ac and merge-base membership; any Prefer-A carve that softens those is a regression.

## In plain English
The gate says you need passing product tests to publish the scope that authorizes writing those product files. That is the pain. We want a thin, shape-bound activation carve and keep real product acceptance hard afterward.

role: critic

audit-targets: none

## In plain English
Prefer-A is the right direction, but cannot bind as drafted. Publish the scope without claiming that its future implementation passed acceptance; keep acceptance unchanged and run it for product delivery. Before bind, define the complete change set that proves activation and replace the ambiguous test-command targeting rule. Otherwise a local product change can be missed, or the reported npm commands can remain blocked.

Round 1; fresh critic; refutation charter. Inputs: issue body, Prefer-A 6352358524, triage 6352358809, and deposit 6352443547 only. Inclusive ceiling: 6352443547. Verification was pin-read at c7e79fe08ea94d4fb22f09320f0e4c7ac58ab5c4, not an executed consumer reproduction. No sibling comments read.

## Existing mechanisms
- [pr-closing-keywords/main.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/c7e79fe08ea94d4fb22f09320f0e4c7ac58ab5c4/packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/main.ts): isBriefLandShapedDiff rejects an empty set, checks destination AND previousFilename against the allowlist, and requires a nonremoved nonterminal brief. It is a shape predicate. evaluatePathBActivationAdmit separately rejects removed briefs, parses each changed brief, checks productPullRequest is unset, and binds issue refs to deft-story marks. Reuse the vocabulary; do not mistake the predicate for all admission checks.
- [cached-orchestrator.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/c7e79fe08ea94d4fb22f09320f0e4c7ac58ab5c4/packages/core/src/check/cached-orchestrator.ts): verify:ac is product-first and fail-fast, soft-empty is not green, pressure can make hygiene advisory, and rapid has a separate zero-verified rejection after a successful AC gate.
- [verify-ac/clauses.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/c7e79fe08ea94d4fb22f09320f0e4c7ac58ab5c4/packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts): declared-scope clause walking explicitly fails a missing positive artifact. [literal-acceptance/run.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/c7e79fe08ea94d4fb22f09320f0e4c7ac58ab5c4/packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/run.ts) executes commands with their existing cwd/output expectations and preserves safety refusals. [verify-ac/evaluate.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/c7e79fe08ea94d4fb22f09320f0e4c7ac58ab5c4/packages/core/src/verify-ac/evaluate.ts) emits actual command-walk outcomes under scope-specific identities; a deferral is not a product pass.
- [write-fence.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/c7e79fe08ea94d4fb22f09320f0e4c7ac58ab5c4/packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts): loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase reads the selected relative path at the resolved merge-base SHA; it does not resolve a pending-path predecessor by plan.id. [scope-provenance.md](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/c7e79fe08ea94d4fb22f09320f0e4c7ac58ab5c4/content/docs/scope-provenance.md) already specifies the committed + working-tree + untracked union, Path B's unset product stamp, and separate immutable membership authority.

## F1 — blocks-the-design: scope-only proof needs one complete change set
Evidence: the draft says “working tree / PR diff brief-land only”; the helper consumes caller-supplied paths and cannot establish completeness. Existing scope-provenance documentation explicitly unions base...HEAD, HEAD-to-working-tree, and untracked paths. The helper also needs rename origins.
Failure mode: a committed product change with only a dirty brief, or a brief-only PR with an untracked product test, can qualify if either surface is used alone. Selecting one unstamped scope also cannot certify other changed briefs. In a shared worktree, a sibling writer can invalidate a previously computed disposition.
Disposition consequence: block bind until admission uses the complete local change set (and the corresponding reviewed diff in CI), preserves rename origins/deletions, ties the selected scope to that activation set, and validates the relevant changed briefs. Missing/failed diff evidence must not produce deferral. Scope prose, environment selection, or an agent-authored “activation” assertion is not proof. Keep the existing merge-base membership/write fence hard; an AC disposition must never widen it. This is a caller contract around the existing shape helper, not a new path dialect.

## F2 — blocks-the-design: “commands that target not-yet-landed paths” is not an executable admission rule
Evidence: the reported commands are npm test and npm run test:coverage, with no product paths in their strings and no scripts yet present. The existing command runner executes commands and compares outcomes; the clause walker has artifact paths, but that does not establish command dependency graphs.
Failure mode: conservative command matching leaves this exact consumer blocked; guessing from missing scripts/stderr can excuse unrelated command failures. Running commands first and forgiving failures also permits side effects before the purported activation-only check.
Disposition consequence: replace selective failure forgiveness with an explicit pre-execution activation disposition for the selected scope's product command/clause execution after deterministic activation admission. Preserve acceptance structure, provenance/safety validation, and applicable scope/document checks. Do not rewrite commands, fabricate clause verification, or emit product-oracle pass evidence. A mixed/product diff or a product stamp must take the unchanged execution path. If selective command deferral is retained instead, bind a concrete classification rule that handles these opaque npm commands; the present wording is insufficient.

## F3 — sharpens-framing: activation disposition must compose with check modes
Evidence: cached-orchestrator applies mode filtering before iteration, permits advisory hygiene in pressure mode, and separately rejects zero verified clauses in rapid mode. The draft promises hygiene and scope-provenance remain hard.
Failure mode: merely returning successful verify:ac can still leave activation red under rapid mode; merely skipping it can produce a green activation while required validation was filtered out or made advisory. Neither implements the promised disposition.
Disposition consequence: retain A, but state that activation runs its required validation hard in every supported check mode and records a named non-product disposition. Test full/pressure/rapid admission and rejection through the real orchestrator; a command-level mock alone does not prove consumer recovery. Do not relax rapid product completion or general hygiene policy.

## F4 — sharpens-framing: landing a pending brief is not runtime activation continuity
Evidence: loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase loads the exact selected path; the shared brief-land helper admits proposed, pending, and active paths. The issue explicitly distinguishes merge-time continuity from runtime loading.
Failure mode: a pending-only publication goes green, then moving that brief to active still leaves its selected active path absent at merge base. Likewise, landing an activation on the delivery branch does not move an older implementation branch's merge base automatically. The consumer remains unable to write despite a successful scope review.
Disposition consequence: keep write-fence.ts unchanged and scope the supported recovery to landing the concrete active-path brief, then starting/rebasing the implementation branch so that activation is actually in its merge base. Require a lifecycle regression that first proves missing-at-base denial, then authorized initial source/test writes, then failing product AC remains blocking. Keep same-PR file_scope widening plus product writes negative. Pending-to-active loader continuity is a separate design unless explicitly added and proven.

## Road not taken / strongest objection
Keeping verify:ac unconditional is strongest when a check is evidence of product completion: it prevents false green acceptance and preserves oracle integrity. It fails here because publication of the precommitment precedes permission to create the measured artifact. That objection would flip my verdict if the activation disposition could be reused as completion evidence or survive a product diff. Approach B loses the acceptance contract during bootstrap; Approach C changes write authority unnecessarily. A deterministic activation admission with an honest non-product disposition is narrower than either.

## Short bindable mechanism
1. Prove complete brief-land activation and selected-scope eligibility with the shared shape vocabulary; failed proof gets no deferral.
2. Defer product execution before running it, preserve the acceptance contract, and run required activation validation hard with an honest disposition.
3. Restore unchanged product acceptance on product/stamped changes; prove exact-active-path merge-base recovery without changing write authority.

Verdict: amend A for F1/F2 before bind; incorporate F3/F4 as explicit scope and validation statements.

## Verdict
Prefer-A Approach A is the right direction (reuse isBriefLandShapedDiff, keep merge-base write-fence immutable, reject Approach C). As drafted it cannot bind. Three blockers must remint into short Bound limbs before Approach A is safe for consumers. Several sharpens keep the carve Thin Fail-Closed.

## Mechanism inventory (tip c7e79fe0)
- isBriefLandShapedDiff (packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/main.ts): allowlist-only; every path (+ rename source) is nonterminal xbrief|vbrief under proposed|pending|active or exact root CHANGELOG.md; requires >=1 non-removed nonterminal brief.
- evaluatePathBActivationAdmit / evaluateFullStoryMarkAdmission (same file): fuller Path B witness — brief-land shape + no deleted nonterminals + deft-story coverage + productPullRequest unset on every changed brief. Closing-keywords early-return only; does not speak to verify:ac.
- loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase (packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts): runtime fence from merge-base brief bytes only; missing-at-base yields empty fileScope (P2 cycle). Cite-only keep-out of head widen is correct.
- verify:ac product path (packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts + literal-acceptance/run.ts + verify-ac/clauses.ts): hard-fails on (1) literal acceptance-command gate when stated commands miss scripts/exit, and (2) clause walk artifact missing at stated path. Observed bullhorn failure is both limbs. none_stated:true with non-empty derived commands still runs those commands. Check composition puts product AC first (cached-orchestrator.ts / #3284) and fail-closes before hygiene.
- Docs Path B (#5387) in content/docs/scope-provenance.md: defines brief-land + unset productPullRequest for membership/closing-keywords; no activation-time verify:ac disposition (P3).

## Findings

### F1 — Local check has no named brief-land inventory source
classification: blocks-the-design
evidence: Prefer-A says working tree / PR diff brief-land only but isBriefLandShapedDiff consumes PrDiffPath[]. Tip closing-keywords uses PR file lists; local DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE=… deft check (the observed consumer path) has no named adapter from status/diff to that shape. Envelope Reject already bans a second brief-land vocabulary.
failure mode: Without a single inventory function (e.g. merge-base..HEAD plus staged/unstaged/untracked mapped into PrDiffPath, or an existing check seam that already builds that list), the carve either never fires on the bullhorn sequence, or fires while untracked src/ / test/ / package.json sit beside the brief and silently skip product AC.
disposition consequence: Bound must name one reuse path: call isBriefLandShapedDiff on a concrete inventory helper already owned by check/closing-keywords, or add a thin adapter in draft file_scope that only maps paths to PrDiffPath and delegates. Do not invent a parallel allowlist regex.

### F2 — Dual AC disposition tokens (named skip or deferred-until-product)
classification: blocks-the-design
evidence: Prefer-A Approach A offers two honest dispositions. Tip already has soft_empty / empty-resolution (#3334), advisory check-integrated paths, and none_stated empty-command soft paths. Consumer brief already carries none_stated:true with non-empty derived npm test / test:coverage — emptying commands (Approach B) is rejected; Prefer-A must not leave two skip dialects.
failure mode: Implementers pick different tokens per call site; check stdout, run-summary, and later product re-entry disagree on whether AC was waived, deferred, or soft-empty. Pain P1 relief becomes non-deterministic.
disposition consequence: Bind exactly one disposition token (recommend one named activation skip/deferred code with exit 0 from check only under the shape witness) and require full verify:ac (commands + clauses) once the witness fails. Docs/alias wording stays footnote.

### F3 — Activation predicate weaker than the existing Path B witness
classification: blocks-the-design
evidence: Prefer-A predicates on productPullRequest unset + brief-land shape. Tip evaluatePathBActivationAdmit also refuses deleted nonterminals, requires deft-story coverage of each changed nonterminal, and treats malformed productPullRequest as not-unset. Swarm/injection lens: an agent can unset the stamp and stage only the brief while product paths remain untracked or on another index state if inventory is weak (pairs with F1).
failure mode: Check softens on a partial looks-like-activation signal that closing-keywords would still refuse, creating a split-brain Path B admit between publish stamps and local check.
disposition consequence: Prefer-A Bound should reuse the existing Path B activation witness predicates (or an exported shared helper from that module) for the check carve, not a thinner productPullRequest-only test. Keep write-fence merge-base loader cite-only.

### F4 — Carve must cover both verify:ac limbs
classification: sharpens-framing
evidence: Observed gate output fails clause walk (artifact missing at stated path on src/record-reference.js / test/record-reference.test.js) and literal command gate (Missing script: test / test:coverage). Prefer-A prose mentions missing future product artifacts or acceptance commands but draft Bound limbs are not explicit that both walkAcceptanceClauses failure and runLiteralAcceptanceCommands failure are in-scope for the single disposition.
failure mode: A commands-only skip still red-fails on clause walk (or the reverse), and the consumer stays blocked.
disposition consequence: One Bound limb must state that under the activation witness, both command-gate and clause-walk hard-fails are replaced by the single disposition; mixed/product diffs keep both hard.

### F5 — Re-arm condition and selected-scope boundary
classification: sharpens-framing
evidence: Prefer-A requires full verify:ac once any product path appears or productPullRequest is set. Check selects one story via DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE / multi-active composition (#4285). Tip product-oracle check_id is already scope-namespaced (#3337).
failure mode: Global check skip when one selected activation-shaped brief is present would waive AC for unrelated product work in the same tree; or carve sticks after product paths land because only productPullRequest was checked.
disposition consequence: Sharpen Bound: carve applies only to the selected scope verify:ac evaluation; witness fails closed if inventory is non-brief-land OR selected brief has productPullRequest set OR any non-allowlisted path is present. Hygiene + scope-provenance membership stay hard (already stated — keep).

### F6 — Future AC retained in brief must still bind product delivery
classification: sharpens-framing
evidence: Prefer-A keeps derived commands/clauses on the activation brief (rejects Approach B empty stamp). Product-oracle integrity fingerprints executed command sets (#3322 / #3397). After activation merges, write fence loads those same merge-base bytes and product writes proceed; later product PR must hard-run the retained commands.
failure mode: Activation skip recorded as a reusable bank/cache green (served_from=bank/cache) could satisfy a later product check without re-execution.
disposition consequence: Bound should forbid serving the activation disposition as a verified-pass bank/cache hit for a later non-activation witness; product path must execute commands/clauses anew.

### F7 — soft_empty / none_stated message collision
classification: footnote
evidence: Tip #3334 soft_empty and none_stated empty-command messaging already exist; consumer brief mixes none_stated:true with non-empty commands.
failure mode: Operators misread activation disposition as empty-AC soft_empty and weaken commands.
disposition consequence: Implementation note — distinct stdout token; no mechanism change.

### F8 — Docs Path B pointer
classification: footnote
evidence: content/docs/scope-provenance.md Path B section documents closing-keywords brief-land only (P3).
failure mode: Docs lag after mechanism lands.
disposition consequence: Pointer sentence after mechanism; harvest-changed:false unless limb title needed for discoverability.

## Steelmans / accepts
- Reject Approach C (head-brief write authority) — tip loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase + #4956 are load-bearing; Prefer-A correctly preserves them.
- Reuse isBriefLandShapedDiff rather than a second dialect — correct Thin Fail-Closed instinct; F1/F3 only demand the call-site witness be complete.
- Keep hygiene + scope-provenance hard; keep mixed scope+product on full verify:ac — necessary for P4.
- Keep future product AC on the brief instead of Approach B empty mint — better consumer continuity if F6 is locked.

## Bind readiness
Cannot bind Prefer-A draft 6352358524 as written. Remint Approach A Bound with short limbs that (1) name the brief-land inventory to isBriefLandShapedDiff adapter, (2) pick one AC disposition token covering command+clause limbs, (3) reuse the fuller Path B activation witness, (4) selected-scope-only + re-arm on product path or productPullRequest, (5) forbid activation disposition as later verified-pass cache. Reject list already good; keep Approach C and second-dialect bans.

## In plain English
Approach A is the right idea: let a true brief-only Path B activation clear check without pretending future product tests already pass, and keep real product acceptance hard afterward. ## Summary

Scope activation requires future tests before merge-base write authority exists

## Context

Consumer: 3Ci-Consulting/bullhorn-mcp on macOS, Codex, Node 24.20.0. After the framework-only coverage blocker in #5791, the operator explicitly requested a simple class and test to produce genuine coverage. The intended change is one RecordReference data container, a node:test serialization assertion, and c8 coverage scripts. Bullhorn requirements remain stashed; no API integration or unresolved architecture decisions are part of this change.

Version boundary: the shared global CLI and implementation checkout report engine/package 0.126.2. The isolated scope-review checkout was created from the delivery branch, which still pins 0.126.1; it was not upgraded merely to publish the scope. The check below was invoked through the global 0.126.2 CLI in that checkout. This report discloses that local pin difference rather than claiming a clean all-0.126.2 end-to-end reproduction.

## Expected behavior

Provide a supported, reviewable bootstrap path for a new implementation scope: validate and review its concrete file_scope and acceptance contract before product writes are authorized, then require the unchanged product acceptance commands once implementation exists. A scope-only activation must not have to claim that future product code already passes its tests. Preserve immutable merge-base authority, fail-closed write checks, applicable scope/document validation, and full acceptance testing for mixed/product changes. The report does not prescribe trusting an agent-widened working-tree brief or a blanket test exemption.

## Actual behavior / gap

The intended recovery forms a cycle: product writes need governing scope at merge base; landing that scope requires the not-yet-written product's acceptance tests.

Observed sequence:
1. Create the new xBRIEF with stable plan.id record-reference-coverage, explicit concrete file_scope covering src/record-reference.js, test/record-reference.test.js, package files and lifecycle paths; promote and activate it through native CLI verbs. xbrief:preflight and scope-provenance validation pass.
2. Attempt the initial source/test writes in the 0.126.2 implementation checkout. The live Directive tool hook denies them. After native scope:block removes the stale setup brief from eligibility, the new scope is selected but still has no positive governing allow coverage at merge base. No source/test files are written.
